input.quote: Vendor exclusively owns every Deliverable created for Customer. Customer receives a revocable, non-transferable licence to use a Deliverable only during the applicable Order Form term.
input.rationale: Section 14.2 gives Vendor exclusive ownership of every Deliverable created specifically for Customer (as defined in Section 1.4) and leaves Customer only a revocable, non-transferable licence limited to the Order Form term. That fails both the preferred position (Customer owns deliverables, Vendor assigns) and the fallback (perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence to use, modify and sublicense deliverables). The perpetual licence in Section 13.2, cross-referenced by Section 14.3, is expressly limited to software and Vendor Technology embedded in a Deliverable, so it does not cure the revocable, term-limited licence to the Deliverables themselves. Section 14.1 (Customer Data and pre-existing Customer IP) and Section 14.4 (no joint ownership) are satisfactory and left unchanged; the redline is confined to reversing the ownership direction in 14.2 while preserving Vendor's ownership of Vendor Technology.

proposal.summary: Reverse ownership of Deliverables to Customer with Vendor assignment; Vendor Technology remains Vendor's under 14.3/13.2
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We own the work product we pay for, so we have reversed Section 14.2 to vest Deliverables in us with an assignment from Vendor; a revocable, term-limited licence to our own paid-for Deliverables is not something we can accept. Vendor Technology remains Vendor's and continues to be covered by Sections 14.3 and 13.2.

ops.oldText: Vendor exclusively owns every Deliverable created for Customer. Customer receives a revocable, non-transferable licence to use a Deliverable only during the applicable Order Form term.
ops.newText: Customer exclusively owns every Deliverable created for Customer, and Vendor hereby irrevocably assigns to Customer all right, title, and interest, including all intellectual property rights, in each Deliverable upon its creation. Vendor Technology is excluded from this assignment and remains subject to Section 14.3 and the perpetual licence in Section 13.2.
